nom: Lecture 2 (part 2) — Cromwell to the Glorious Revolution
cartes: The Commonwealth: Cromwell abolishes the monarchy
Parliament forbids the celebration of Christmas
Oliver Cromwell massacres Drogheda and Wexford (Ireland)
Cromwell's Act of Settlement: land of Irish Catholics is confiscated ("absentee landlords")
Catholics own 59% of the land in Ireland (under 20% after 1652)
Richard Cromwell, Oliver's son, is Lord Protector
Some MPs invite Charles II (Charles I's son) to return as King
Charles II signs a secret treaty with Louis XIV (to convert England back to Catholicism)
Great Fire of London; 22 people die in anti-Catholic riots
Test Acts: Non-Anglicans excluded from official positions, universities and legal careers
Conflict between Parliament and James (Charles II's openly Catholic brother)
Birth of James II's son, immediately baptised a Catholic
Parliament secretly invites the Protestant William of Orange to take the throne; James II flees to France
James II's armies and Catholic allies are defeated in Ireland
Act of Settlement: a Catholic can no longer sit on the throne of England
Abolition of the Act of Settlement
Bill of Rights Act: Parliament's authority over the sovereign (no laws, taxes or army without Parliament's consent)
James II, Catholic king ousted for his arbitrary rule (life dates)
William III, "William of Orange", Protestant joint monarch (life dates)
Mary II, joint monarch with William III (life dates)
